newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Premier shareholders clear FAI buyback.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Premier shareholders clear FAI buyback.

text.p: Shareholders of investment vehicle Premier Investments Ltd on Tuesday approved the company's A$8.6 million buyback of 16.2 million shares held in the company by the FAI Insurances Ltd.
Premier chief executive, Harry Cooper told shareholders that the shares were being bought at 53 cents a share, a substantial discount to the current share price of 74 cents.
"It's obvious that it's a good deal for Premier and for shareholders," Cooper told the annual meeting in Melbourne.
The share buyback follows Premier's move in October to sell its 15 percent stake in FAI to institutions for A$31.5 million.
Premier is 40 percent owned by Coles Myer Ltd director, Solomon Lew's private investment vehicle, Century Plaza. Lew owns 14 percent of Coles through Premier and Century Plaza.
Premier has said it was likely to use some of the A$20 million in net proceeds from the unwinding of the cross shareholding with FAI to buy more shares in Coles.
Coles shares closed steady at A$4.62.
